A seasonal trade-wind regime is expected to continue across the 
Marianas through at least this weekend, as the trade-wind surge 
builds due to an increasing pressure gradient between the tropics and
the midlatitudes. This trade-wind surge is strong enough to keep the
descending shearline from intruding into the region, pushing it out 
more west of 140E and moreso toward the Philippines. As such, only 
isolated to low-end scattered showers are expected the next several 
days, staying mostly dry for much of next week. As we delve further
into the season and winter settles across east Asia, shearlines are
expected to descend further into the tropics over the coming months,
which may bring periods of refreshing, albeit windier conditions.

Marine...
While current sea conditions are unsettled, recent altimetry, 
scatterometry, and buoy data have yielded seas and winds below the 
required threshold of conditions for a Small Craft Advisory. 
Regardless, there is a high risk of rip currents expected at least 
into the weekend.

Moderate to fresh easterly winds of 15 to 20 knots are expected 
through Saturday evening, with occasional gusts up to 25 knots 
possible. Combined seas of 7 to 9 feet are expected into the weekend 
and may briefly drop a foot around Saturday, before increasing to 
upwards of 10 feet early next week. 

By early next week, a resurgence of trade-wind swell is expected to 
arrive in the region, which will bring elevated and potentially 
hazardous seas to small craft.

Eastern Micronesia...
Not much has changed with our thinking regarding the rapidly
increasing seas and surf area-wide this weekend. This afternoon's
analysis shows the STR (Sub-Tropical Ridge positioned to the north
(near 24N), with moderate to fresh sustained winds of 15 to 20 knots
mainly centered between 10N and 25N. Scatterometry analysis also 
shows fresh to strong winds of 20 to 25 knots east of 145E from 10N 
to 25N. There's even some near gale winds of 25 to 30 knots between 
15N and 20N, east of 175E, with gales between 20N and 25N, also east 
of 175E.

What this all means is significant wave generation is occurring, with
the latest altimetry showing seas of 12 to 15 feet in that core
around 175E, with 9 to 12 feet in the fresh to strong area, and 6 to
9 in the moderate to fresh. Keep in mind these wave heights are just
starting to build, and unlike the FSM (Federated States of 
Micronesia) and the RMI (Republic of the Marshall Islands), where the
island chains will disrupt the fetch length, there's virtually 
northing to make such disruption northeast of these regions. Thus, 
when the waves arrive, and as a high pressure cell moves east along 
the STR, wave build-ups will be fairly rapid for all of eastern 
Micronesia. At this time, current model forecasts show this occurring
Saturday afternoon or evening from east to west, continuing through 
the weekend. As such, all headlines remain in places, with advisories
likely being issued sometime Friday, barring a radical shift in the 
model data.

Then we have the precipitation challenge, as the scatterometry 
analysis also shows a circulation has formed over Kosrae. 
Additionally, the 6-Layer ALP (ALL-precipitable Water) imagery shows 
the various lows in the 850-300mb layer have basically consolidated 
(there's still some tilted vorticity) southwest of Chuuk/southeast of
Pohnpei. This has allowed convection to encircle Kosrae, with the 
island itself in the cusp of the arcing convection. Still, we expect 
convection to move over Kosrae so we increased shower coverage to 
numerous, with 60 to 70 percent probabilities tonight through 
Saturday, decreasing to scattered/chance coverage/probabilities for 
the first half of next week. Pohnpei will see isolated showers 
tonight increase to scattered Friday night, with increasing 
thunderstorm potential by then as well, with all of this continuing 
into next week. Majuro is "the odd man out," with mainly isolated 
showers expected there.

As for our mariners, as mentioned above, Saturday looks to be the day
when seas rapidly increase from east to west. Seas look to peak in
the 10 to 12 foot range at Majuro, 9 to 11 feet at Pohnpei, and 8 to
10 foot range at Kosrae Sunday or Monday. At least moderate to fresh
winds will develop area-wide, with winds potentially becoming strong
at Majuro and the northern half of the RMI.

Western Micronesia...

showers through Friday night at all forecast locations with isolated
